attorney: lawyer who represents a client in court or legal matters
witness-box: enclosed stand in a courtroom where witnesses give testimony
cross-examine: question a witness closely to test or challenge what they said
testimony: formal statement of evidence given by a witness under oath
verdict: formal decision on guilt or innocence reached by a jury
jurymen: men who sit on a jury and decide a legal case
counsel: lawyer who argues a case in court
foreman: jury member who speaks for the jury and announces its verdict
germane: relevant and appropriate to the matter being discussed
recital: detailed spoken account of events or facts
sordid: dirty, squalid, and morally degraded or unpleasant
meager: scanty, small in amount, or insufficient
whence: from what place, source, or origin
semblance: outward appearance or pretense of something
spendthrift: person who spends money wastefully and recklessly
schooner: sailing ship with two or more masts and fore-and-aft sails
steamer: ship powered by steam engines, often a passenger vessel
liner: large passenger ship sailing on a regular route
gunmen: armed criminals who use guns to commit crimes
sidewalk: paved path beside a street for pedestrians, American usage
roadway: the part of a road used by vehicles
drowsed: dozed or grew sleepy and half-asleep
rat-faced: having a sharp, pointed, unattractive face like a rat
cocoanuts: old spelling of coconuts, fruit of the coconut palm
breadfruit: large starchy tropical fruit eaten like a vegetable
banana-leaves: broad large leaves of the banana plant
cloak: loose outer garment worn over other clothes
fathom: unit of water depth equal to six feet
translucent: allowing light through but not clear enough to see through
thatched: roofed with straw, reeds, or similar plant material
barnacle goose: wild goose of northern regions, once thought to grow from barnacles
chiming: ringing softly and musically, as of bells
stocky: short, solidly built, and thick-set in body
mellow: soft, rich, and pleasantly relaxed in tone or mood
brief: legal document summarizing a case for a lawyer to argue
bench: judge's seat, or the court where judges sit
morbid: unhealthily interested in death, disease, or unpleasant things
clamor: loud, persistent noise or excited shouting
rustle: soft, crisp sound made by moving leaves or paper
bronze: reddish-brown metal alloy, also the colour of that metal
erect: upright, straight, with the body or head held high
ashore: onto or on the land, having left a ship
lagoon: shallow lake of seawater separated from the sea by a reef
unquiet: restless, troubled, or anxious in mind
rapped: knocked sharply and quickly on a surface
loomed: appeared large, dark, and threatening through the mist or dusk
awfully: extremely or very, used as an intensifier in older speech
ain't: dialect contraction meaning am not, is not, or are not
dwelt: lived or resided in a place, past tense of dwell
belle: attractive young woman, especially admired at social gatherings
aright: correctly, rightly, or in the proper way
burgess: citizen or freeman of an old English town, with voting rights
gaiety: cheerful, lively merriment and good spirits
unabashed: not embarrassed, ashamed, or made self-conscious
venue: place where a trial or public event is held
proven: shown to be true by evidence, a legal or Scottish form of proved
hurling: throwing something forcefully and violently through the air
old-time: belonging to former times, old-fashioned or traditional
